common_name: Golden Era Tree Peony (Reath Lutea Hybrid Yellow Tree Peony)

planting.note: Plant container or bare-root shrubs in early to mid fall in deep, humus-rich, well-drained soil in full sun to light afternoon shade, setting a grafted union several inches below the soil surface to encourage the scion to form its own roots.

directions: Golden Era is an advanced-generation lutea hybrid bred by D.L. Reath from a 'Golden Isle' x 'Daphnis' cross, first blooming in 1971, bearing fragrant, heavy-textured yellow flowers marked with reddish-maroon flares at the base of each petal and a light reddish picotee edge along the margins. Each sturdy stem typically carries one to three buds held well above the deeply cut foliage, and the shrub is a fast, vigorous grower that eventually reaches around 5 feet tall, larger than many tree peony cultivars. Because of its strong lutea-hybrid genetics and fertile pollen, Golden Era is frequently used by breeders as a pollen parent for newer intersectional (Itoh) hybrid introductions.

common_name: Black Panther Tree Peony (Saunders Lutea Hybrid Black-Red Tree Peony)

planting.note: Plant container or bare-root shrubs in early to mid fall in deep, humus-rich, well-drained soil in full sun to light afternoon shade, setting a grafted union several inches below the soil surface to encourage the scion to form its own roots.

directions: Black Panther is a Lutea hybrid tree peony bred by A. P. Saunders and introduced in 1948, producing large, semi-double to nearly fully double flowers in the darkest black-red clustered around a boss of golden stamens, carrying a light, spicy-sweet fragrance. Its finely cut, deeply divided foliage emerges blushed red in spring and keeps a delicate, almost bamboo-like texture through the season, and the shrub builds into a compact, semi-spreading mound only about 3 feet tall and wide. It is a late-season bloomer, typically opening in late May to early June, and tolerates a notably wide hardiness range for a tree peony.

common_name: Shimanishiki Tree Peony (Red-and-White Candy-Striped Japanese Tree Peony)

planting.note: Plant container or bare-root shrubs in early to mid fall in deep, humus-rich, well-drained soil in full sun to partial afternoon shade, setting a grafted union several inches below the soil surface to encourage the scion to form its own roots.

directions: Shimanishiki arose as a bud-sport mutation from the red Japanese tree peony 'Taiyo' and is grown for its large, lightly fragrant, candy-striped double flowers that mix red and white in unpredictable patterns around a center of golden stamens. Because it is a genetic chimera, individual blooms and even whole branches can vary from one season to the next, occasionally opening solid red or solid white instead of the typical striped combination. Its deeply divided, medium-green foliage stays attractive through the growing season on a shrub that slowly builds into a multi-stemmed specimen several feet tall and wide.
